conditions.description: Long open-sea voyage requires Tier 3 ship
Player should be established before visiting

travel_note.description: The longest voyage in the early game. Crosses open sea with no landmarks. Navigation skill or a good chart is strongly recommended.

tile_details.description: packed sandy earth mixed with stone paving — newer than Tyre, some areas still being built
the highest point has fine stone construction — Carthage showing its ambition
where the city meets the African land — different building styles, local materials
separate from war harbor — smaller, more chaotic, merchants from Africa and Phoenicia mixed

day.note: Hotter and brighter than anywhere on the Phoenician coast

location.lore_note: Carthage was founded by Phoenicians from Tyre and it remembers its origins — but it is growing into something new and more powerful. It sits at the crossroads between the Mediterranean world and deep Africa. The city has things no Phoenician coast merchant has ever seen: African gold, ivory, exotic animals, and knowledge of lands beyond the Sahara. It also has ambition that makes Tyre nervous.

visual.description: The civilian harbor — separate from the war harbor. Busy and slightly chaotic. African traders and Phoenician sailors share the same dock space uneasily.

buildings.note: Most expensive docking in the game so far — Carthage charges more because it can

visual.description: The most visually striking market in the game. Goods and people from deep Africa that no Phoenician player has seen before. Caged exotic animals, baskets of gold dust, stacks of ivory. Merchants in clothing styles unlike anything on the coast.

inventory.note: Most expensive buyable item in the game at this stage. Sells for enormous profit anywhere on the Phoenician coast.
Dirt cheap here. Worth a fortune to inland African tribes who have never seen glass.

unique_mechanic.name: barter_system
unique_mechanic.description: Some African traders in this market do not use silver. They trade by barter only — exchanging goods for goods. Player can bring Phoenician manufactured goods and trade them directly for African exotics without spending silver.

visual.description: Built by the original Tyrian founders of Carthage. Older than most of the city. Dedicated to Tanit and Baal Hammon — Carthaginian versions of Phoenician gods. The treasure said to be buried beneath this temple is the most persistent rumor in the city.

hidden_mechanic.description: The legendary founders' treasure actually exists in the game. Reaching it requires completing a multi-step quest chain and is one of the largest single rewards in Part 1.

visual.description: Phoenician-built trading house but already showing Carthaginian independence — the decor mixes Tyrian and local African styles.

lines.speaker: hanno_minor
lines.text: You came from the coast. I can tell by the way you're staring at everything.

lines.speaker: hanno_minor
lines.text: Everything here has a price. Even the things that don't look like they're for sale. What did you bring me?

player_choices.text: Ask where the gold comes from
Ask what lies deeper in Africa

lines.speaker: hanno_minor
lines.text: The gold comes from far south. Months of travel south. There are kingdoms there that have never heard of Phoenicia.

lines.speaker: hanno_minor
lines.text: But you don't need to go there. I bring it here. The question is what you bring me in return.

secret.description: Planning a major southward expedition along the African coast — looking for investors. If the player funds it, they receive a share of whatever he finds.

lines.speaker: sophoniba
lines.text: You are a long way from home, merchant. Carthage welcomes those who come to trade. The gods welcome those who come with respect.

lines.speaker: sophoniba
lines.text: Do you know who built this city? A queen who fled Tyre with almost nothing and founded this. Remember that the next time you think your starting point defines your destination.

secret.description: Knows exactly where the founders' treasure is buried beneath the temple. Will reveal it only to someone who has proven genuine connection to Phoenician heritage and has completed a task of real significance.

entry_position.description: Beneath the temple altar — a stone panel that moves when weight is applied in a specific pattern

discovery_triggers.description: Sophoniba tells the player directly after quest unlocks
Multiple market traders mention the treasure as legend

options.description: Damages the altar, lowers Carthage reputation by 25

contents.description: A stone vault with objects from Tyre — brought by the founders when they fled. Phoenician artifacts, sealed jars, and a large cedar chest.

loot.description: Third and final piece of the Map of the Outer Sea. Shows islands in the Atlantic Ocean west of the Pillars of Hercules.
A bronze seal belonging to Carthage's founder. Grants special diplomatic status with Carthage permanently.

reward_summary.significance: Contains the third and final map fragment — completing the Map of the Outer Sea and enabling Phase 3 of the Legendary Voyage

steps.description: Fund Hanno's southward expedition along the African coast
Hanno departs — player can do other things during this time
Return after 10 days to collect the share

reward.description: Player receives 700 silver profit share plus a map showing a new African coastal location for Part 2
reward.note: Net profit of 400 silver on the 300 investment — teaches investment mechanic

steps.description: Sophoniba asks the player to bring one item that proves their connection to Phoenician heritage

reward.note: Completing this quest means the player has all 3 map fragments and can now begin the final voyage preparation

economy.note: Carthage has the most exotic and highest-value goods in the game. The barter system means players who bring the right Phoenician goods can acquire African exotics without spending silver at all — a major economic shortcut.
